headline: Deep underground, heat and pressure transform ordinary elements into extraordinary treasures
universal_truth: Pressure and time transform the ordinary into the extraordinary
fun_facts: Diamonds form 100 miles underground under extreme heat and pressure
Gold is so rare that all the gold ever mined would fit in a 70-foot cube
Some minerals form in volcanic vents; others require millions of years of compression
discussion_questions: What pressure in your life has created something valuable?
Why do we value rare minerals so highly?
What ordinary thing in your life might be 'treasure' to someone else?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Beneath your feet lie treasures: gold, diamonds, sapphires, rubies—forged by forces we can barely imagine. Extreme heat. Crushing pressure. Millions of years. The same elements that make up dirt become gems under the right conditions. Transformation requires intensity.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Carbon is one of the most common elements on Earth. So why are diamonds—made of pure carbon—so valuable? What transforms ordinary carbon into the hardest, most brilliant natural material on Earth?

options.text: Extreme pressure and heat 100 miles underground rearranges carbon atoms
options.response: Yes. At 100 miles deep, pressure forces carbon into a perfect crystal lattice—a diamond.

options.text: Volcanic eruptions crystallize carbon as it cools rapidly
options.response: Volcanoes bring diamonds up, but they're formed much deeper...

q1.title: Diamond Formation
q1.script: Diamonds form about 100 miles underground, where pressure is 725,000 pounds per square inch and temperatures reach 2,000°F. Volcanic eruptions then rocket them to the surface in hours. The journey from deep Earth takes millions of years; the final trip takes hours.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Diamond Formation"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Rare Gold
q2.script: All the gold ever mined in human history—from Egyptian pharaohs to modern mines—would fit in a cube about 70 feet on each side. Gold is rare because it's created in supernovas and neutron star collisions. Earth's gold was delivered by asteroid impacts.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Endless Variety
q3.script: Over 5,000 minerals have been identified—each requiring specific conditions to form. Some crystallize from volcanic heat, others from evaporating seas, others from biological processes. The diversity of Earth's treasures reflects the diversity of its conditions.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Extraordinary things emerge from ordinary materials under extraordinary conditions. Pressure, heat, and time don't destroy—they transform. What feels like crushing pressure might be forging your diamond.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 68. Tomorrow, we'll discover how gems are made. Until then, consider: what pressure in your life might be transforming you into something more valuable?
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Pressure to Diamond - Reframe Intensity
growTrack.learning_objective: See difficult conditions as potentially transformative
growTrack.activity: Identify a period of intense pressure in your life—past or present. Instead of seeing it as merely hard, ask: what is this pressure creating? What ordinary parts of me might be transforming into something more valuable?
